scope: Theorem 1.2 (General diagonal maps on a sheet) of the manuscript “Geometric Programs for Solenoidal Forcing” (preprints/Geometric-Programs-for-Solenoidal-Forcing-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1e54090582721ee2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Pi, Qi ⊂ [2, 3]2, 1 ≤ i ≤ N, be closed rectangles with rational vertices and positive side lengths. Suppose the sources are pairwise positively separated and the targets are pairwise positively separated. Let Fi : Pi → Qi be the center-to-center affine map with any positive rational diagonal linear part, with Fi(Pi) = Qi. For each computable ν > 0 there is an effective smooth mean-zero solenoidal force on T3 10, one-periodic from time zero, whose unique solution in the classical class has pressure zero and period map (y, 2) 7−→ (Fi(y), 2) (y ∈ Pi). Its velocity is zero near integer times and has zero self-advection; all mixed derivatives of force and velocity are bounded. No condition is imposed on source–target intersections. For N = 0 use zero.
